455:     """Extract a compact per-epoch epidemic/contamination series from history.
456: 
457:     Keeps only the scalar fields needed for epidemic curves, detection lag,
458:     contamination spread and cost-effectiveness analysis — not the full
459:     per-agent / per-zone records — so it stays ~50 KB per run.
460: 
461:     ``new_infections`` is the per-epoch incidence estimator
462:     ``max(0, (I+R)_t − (I+R)_{t−1})``.
463:     """
464:     series: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
465:     prev_ever_infected = 0
466:     for epoch_idx, rec in enumerate(history):
467:         s = record_block(rec, RECORD_SUMMARY)
468:         cost = record_block(rec, RECORD_COST_ACCOUNTING)
469:         spaces = record_spaces(rec)

282: def _burst(epochs: list[int], window: int) -> tuple[float, float | None]:
283:     """Max share of epochs inside any rolling `window`-epoch window.
284: 
285:     Returns (share, centre epoch of the densest window). Two-pointer over
286:     sorted epochs, O(n log n).

288:     if not epochs:

291:     best, best_lo = 0, 0
292:     j = 0

144:     blob: bytes,
145: ) -> tuple[list[int], list[int], bytes, bool]:
146:     """Stream-decompress the census member once.
147: 
148:     Returns (all onboard acquisition epochs, cs-route acquisition epochs,
149:     rolling tail window, saw-cs-marker) — the acquisition regex runs per
150:     chunk on a small overlap, and the tail window keeps the trailing
151:     `common_source` block for the tail-decode. Baseline arms emit no
152:     `common_source` block at all, so the marker flag is what tells a
153:     legitimately empty witness from a window that ran short.
154:     """
155:     dec = zlib.decompressobj(16 + zlib.MAX_WBITS)
156:     acq_all: list[int] = []
157:     cs_acq: list[int] = []
158:     prev = b""
159:     tail = b""
160:     saw_marker = False

162:     # host rows must not trip this (ind arms have cs acquisitions but the
163:     # witness block itself may be absent)

170: @dataclass(frozen=True)
171: class SimClock:
172:     """Converts epoch counts to the day-valued scale pathogen profiles use."""
173: 
174:     epoch_duration_hours: float = DEFAULT_EPOCH_DURATION_HOURS
175:     mode: str = LEGACY_EPOCH_DAY
176: 
177:     def __post_init__(self) -> None:
178:         if self.mode not in MODES:
179:             raise ValueError(f"unknown natural-history clock mode: {self.mode!r}")
180:         if not math.isfinite(self.epoch_duration_hours):
181:             raise ValueError(
182:                 "epoch_duration_hours must be finite, got "
183:                 f"{self.epoch_duration_hours}",
184:             )
185:         if self.epoch_duration_hours <= 0:
186:             raise ValueError(
187:                 f"epoch_duration_hours must be positive, got {self.epoch_duration_hours}",
188:             )
189: 
190:     # ── epochs → wall clock ───────────────────────────────────────────────
191: 
192:     @property
193:     def hours_per_epoch(self) -> float:
194:         """Wall-clock hours one epoch spans.
195: 
196:         Under the legacy clock an epoch *is* a day of natural history, so a
197:         physical delay must be read on that same day-long grid — otherwise the
198:         control arm gets a 72-epoch (72-day) microbiology turnaround while its
199:         biology still advances a day per epoch, which is not the pre-clock
200:         behaviour it exists to reproduce.
201:         """
202:         if self.mode == LEGACY_EPOCH_DAY:
203:             return HOURS_PER_DAY
204:         return self.epoch_duration_hours
205: 
206:     def hours_elapsed(self, epochs: float) -> float:
207:         """Wall-clock hours spanned by ``epochs`` epochs."""
208:         return float(epochs) * self.hours_per_epoch
209: 
210:     @property
211:     def day_fraction_per_epoch(self) -> float:
212:         """Fraction of a natural-history day represented by one epoch."""
213:         return self.hours_per_epoch / HOURS_PER_DAY
214: 
215:     def amount_per_epoch(self, amount_per_day: float) -> float:
216:         """Convert a per-day amount to the amount for one epoch."""
217:         if self.mode == LEGACY_EPOCH_DAY:
218:             return float(amount_per_day)
219:         return float(amount_per_day) * self.day_fraction_per_epoch

32:   specimens tested; **92 of 95 were norovirus (96.8%** of tested outbreaks —
33:   the paper prints both 97% and "92%"; the count is 92/95). All 87
34:   viral-only outbreaks were norovirus, plus 4 mixed viral-bacterial and 1
35:   mixed viral-parasitic. Non-norovirus etiologies in the period:
36:   enterotoxigenic *E. coli* (6 outbreaks), *Shigella sonnei* (1),
37:   *Campylobacter jejuni* (1), *Clostridium perfringens* (1, crew-only),
38:   *Cyclospora cayetanensis* (1). As a share of all 133 reported outbreaks
39:   (including untested), norovirus is 69.2%.
40: - **Preston et al. 2026**, *Open Forum Infectious Diseases* 13, DOI
41:   10.1093/ofid/ofaf695.2359 (`Ab`, conference abstract, CDC data): **since
42:   2019, 81% of cruise-ship AGE outbreaks posted to the VSP website were
43:   attributed to norovirus**; GII.17 has become the predominant genotype over
44:   GII.4 in 2020–2025.
45: - **Cramer et al. 2003**, *MMWR* 51(49):1112–5, DOI 10.1001/jama.289.2.167
46:   (`Ab`): 2002 season — 21 outbreaks reported, **9 confirmed norovirus**, 3
47:   bacterial, 9 unknown etiology → 75% of the 12 etiology-determined outbreaks,
48:   43% of all reported. 2001: 4 of 7 outbreaks norovirus.
49: - **Cramer et al. 2004**, *J Infect Dis* 190(1), DOI 10.1086/420888 (`Ab`,
50:   `Me`): of 14 laboratory-confirmed cruise outbreaks in 2002, 12 (85.7%) were
51:   calicivirus, of which 11 were norovirus → **78.6% of confirmed outbreaks**.
52: - **Scaioli et al. 2013**, *Eur J Public Health* 23, DOI
53:   10.1093/eurpub/ckt123.192 (`Sec`, abstract citing CDC): "over 90% of
54:   diarrheal disease outbreaks on cruise ships are caused by norovirus".
55: - **Mouchtouri et al. 2024**, *Eurosurveillance* 29(10), DOI
56:   10.2807/1560-7917.es.2024.29.10.2300345 (`Ab`): norovirus has been the
57:   **leading cause of AGE outbreaks on cruise ships since 2006**.
58: 
59: **Synthesis:** across four surveillance eras the norovirus share of
60: etiology-determined cruise outbreaks sits in **~0.75–0.97**; the recent-era
61: point is ~0.81–0.97. The credible interval for "an outbreak posted to VSP is
62: norovirus" is **~0.8–0.95**.
63: 
64: ## 3. Case-level aboard ship — partly measured
65: 
66: - **Freeland et al. 2016** (`R`): 129,678 passenger AGE cases in 2008–2014,
67:   of which only **19,273 (14.9%) were part of an outbreak**; of those
68:   outbreak-associated cases, **13,568 (70.4%) were in laboratory-confirmed
69:   norovirus outbreaks**. Crew: 43,132 AGE cases, 1,984 (4.6%)
70:   outbreak-associated, of which 1,343 (67.7%) in confirmed norovirus
71:   outbreaks.
72:   → **Measured floor:** norovirus outbreak cases are ≥10.5% of *all*
73:   passenger AGE cases and ≥3.1% of all crew AGE cases. The etiology of the
74:   remaining ~85–95% (non-outbreak presentations) was never tested.
75: - **Wikswo et al. 2011**, *Clin Infect Dis* 52(9):1116–22, DOI
76:   10.1093/cid/cir144 (`Ab`): within one high-morbidity 2009 outbreak,
77:   **12/14 (85.7%) tested specimens were norovirus-positive**; 15.4% of
78:   surveyed passengers met the AGE case definition and **40% of them never
79:   reported to the infirmary** — infirmary surveillance detected only 60% of
80:   AGE cases. Relevant to any "fleet AGE" denominator built on reported cases.
